Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea (5–6/day) following brief vomiting; no blood or abdominal pain. Clinician impression: acute gastroenteritis; supportive care advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhea for 3 days, approximately 5–6 times/day.
- Course: Began with vomiting (a couple of episodes), which has resolved; diarrhea ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: Feels dehydrated and weak; poor appetite; felt mildly warm at onset, now feels fine.
- Pertinent negatives: No visible blood in stool; no abdominal pain; no headaches or myalgias.
- Exposures: No recalled questionable/takeaway food; no known sick contacts.
- Past medical history: Asthma.
- Medications: “Blue” inhaler (short-acting bronchodilator); dose/route/frequency not documented. No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father—hypertension; died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago. Mother—type 2 diabetes.
- Social: Lives alone; software engineer; non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially/infrequently; off work for 3 days due to illness.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis.

Plan:
- Hydration: Encourage ample oral fluids; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as discussed.
- Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) for feverish feeling/weakness.
- Activity/work: Continue time off work for the next day or two; return once diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.
- Follow-up: If not improving by next week, return for reassessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; physical exam (including hydration status and abdominal exam); travel history; recent antibiotic use or hospitalization; detailed stool characteristics beyond “watery;” exact inhaler name and dose/frequency; immunization status; formal medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor hesitations/inaudible segments but key clinical details understandable.
